newsitem.title: USA: CardioVascular Dynamics starts infant trial.
newsitem.headline: CardioVascular Dynamics starts infant trial.

text.p: CardioVascular Dynamics Inc said it has begun a worldwide clinical trial to study its vascular access technology in critically ill infants.

The technology involves the use of a tiny doppler ultrasound crystal placed at the tip of a conventional vascular access needle or catheter. CardioVascular Dynamics has miniaturized the chip to nine thousandths of an inch, which it said should be small enough to locate blood vessels in small infants.

The company believes that this technology, named P.D. Access, will provide quicker, more accurate and safer vascular access in young infants (as young as one-day old) undergoing surgical procedures, pediatric intensive care treatment and in neonatal procedures.
The company said that if trials are successful the U.S. product launch could begin by late 1997.
